q: Which state has the highest kinetic energy of particles?
solution: Gas particles move fastest and have the most kinetic energy.

q: The heat required to change 1 kg of ice at 0 °C into water at 0 °C is called:
solution: Latent heat of fusion melts the ice without changing temperature.

q: Why does evaporation cause cooling?
solution: The fastest particles escape as vapour, taking away energy and lowering the average kinetic energy (temperature) of what remains.

topic: The Gaseous State and the SI Units
q: 0 °C equals:
solution: Kelvin temperature = Celsius + 273.15.

topic: The Gaseous State and the SI Units
q: Gases are highly compressible because:
solution: Large inter-particle spaces allow compression.
options: There is a lot of space between particles

topic: The Gaseous State and the SI Units
q: Convert 27 °C to kelvin.
Which is a homogeneous mixture?
solution: Salt dissolves to give a uniform composition.

q: Which mixture shows the Tyndall effect?
solution: Colloidal particles scatter light.

q: Distinguish between a solution and a suspension.
solution: In a solution the solute is dissolved and does not settle; a suspension has larger particles that settle on standing.

q: Which is a compound?
solution: Water contains hydrogen and oxygen chemically combined.

q: A magnet can separate:
solution: Iron is magnetic and can be pulled out.

q: How would you separate a mixture of alcohol and water?
solution: By fractional distillation, because the two liquids have different boiling points.

topic: Laws of Chemical Combination and Atomic Mass
q: Avogadro's number is:
solution: One mole of any substance contains 6.022 × 1023 particles.

topic: Laws of Chemical Combination and Atomic Mass
q: The law of conservation of mass was proposed by:
solution: Antoine Lavoisier established the law of conservation of mass.

topic: Writing Chemical Formulas and Mole Calculations
q: Volume of 1 mole of an ideal gas at STP is:
solution: One mole occupies 22.4 L at STP.

topic: Writing Chemical Formulas and Mole Calculations
q: Calculate the percentage of oxygen in water.
solution: Oxygen mass = 16 out of 18, so (16/18) × 100 ≈ 88.9%.

q: The mass number of an atom is:
solution: Mass number counts protons plus neutrons.

q: Which experiment led to the discovery of the nucleus?
solution: Alpha particles scattering showed a small dense nucleus.

q: What are isotopes? Give one example.
solution: Atoms of the same element with different numbers of neutrons; for example chlorine-35 and chlorine-37.

q: The maximum number of electrons in the L shell is:
solution: The L shell holds up to 8 electrons.

q: Valency is:
solution: Valency reflects how many electrons an atom can gain, lose or share.
options: The combining capacity of an element

q: Write the electronic configuration of chlorine and state its valency.
solution: 2, 8, 7; valency 1 (it gains one electron).

q: Which organelle is called the powerhouse of the cell?
solution: Mitochondria release energy as ATP.

q: Prokaryotic cells lack:
solution: Their DNA is not enclosed in a nucleus.

q: Why is the plasma membrane called selectively permeable?
solution: It allows only certain substances to pass in or out of the cell.

topic: Cell Division and the Cell Theory
q: Cells that are genetically identical to the parent are produced by:
solution: Mitosis produces identical daughter cells.

topic: Cell Division and the Cell Theory
q: Meiosis produces:
solution: Meiosis gives four haploid gametes.

topic: Cell Division and the Cell Theory
q: State the cell theory.
solution: All organisms are made of cells; the cell is the basic unit of life; all cells arise from pre-existing cells.

q: Which tissue transports food in plants?
solution: Phloem carries sugars from leaves to other parts.

q: Meristematic tissue is responsible for:
solution: It contains actively dividing cells.

q: Differentiate xylem and phloem.
solution: Xylem carries water and minerals upward and is mostly dead; phloem carries food in both directions and is living.

q: Which tissue connects muscle to bone?
solution: Tendons attach muscle to bone; ligaments join bone to bone.

q: Voluntary muscles are found in the:
solution: Skeletal muscles are under conscious control.

q: Name the four types of animal tissue.
solution: Epithelial, connective, muscular and nervous tissue.

q: Which kingdom includes bacteria?
solution: Bacteria are prokaryotes in kingdom Monera.

q: Binomial nomenclature uses:
solution: The scientific name has two parts: genus and species.

q: Write the hierarchy of classification from kingdom to species.
solution: Kingdom -> phylum -> class -> order -> family -> genus -> species.

q: Which group has naked seeds?
solution: Gymnosperm seeds are not enclosed in a fruit.

q: Which vertebrate group has moist skin and lays eggs in water?
solution: Amphibians such as frogs depend on water for reproduction.

q: Name the five vertebrate groups.
solution: Fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals.

q: Displacement can be:
solution: On a closed loop displacement is zero, though distance is not.
options: Zero while distance is not zero

q: The SI unit of acceleration is:
solution: Acceleration is velocity change per unit time.

q: A cyclist covers 20 km in 1 hour. Find the average speed.
solution: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time = 20 ÷ 1 = 20 km/h.

q: The area under a velocity-time graph gives:
solution: Area under v-t graph = displacement.

solution: Force equals mass times acceleration.

q: A body at rest stays at rest unless:
solution: This is the law of inertia.

q: Calculate the force needed to accelerate a 5 kg mass at 3 m/s^2^.
The SI unit of momentum is:
solution: Momentum is mass times velocity, kg·m/s.

q: Momentum is conserved when:
solution: Conservation holds for isolated systems.

q: Why are airbags safer than rigid dashboards?
solution: They increase the collision time, reducing the force on the passenger.

q: The value of G is:
solution: G is the universal gravitational constant.

q: Weight of a 10 kg object on Earth (g = 9.8) is:
State the universal law of gravitation.
solution: Every particle attracts every other with a force proportional to the product of masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance.

topic: Free Fall, Motion of Planets and Satellites
q: g near Earth's surface is about:
solution: Earth's surface gravity is about 9.8 m/s2.

topic: Free Fall, Motion of Planets and Satellites
q: Escape velocity from Earth is about:
solution: An object needs about 11.2 km/s to escape Earth's gravity.

topic: Free Fall, Motion of Planets and Satellites
q: Why does a satellite not fall to Earth?
solution: Its high tangential velocity makes it fall around Earth rather than into it.

q: The SI unit of work is the:
solution: Work and energy are measured in joules.

q: If speed doubles, kinetic energy becomes:
solution: KE ∝ v2, so doubling speed quadruples kinetic energy.

q: A 10 kg object is lifted 2 m. Find the work done (g = 9.8 m/s^2^).
Energy is:
solution: Total energy stays constant, though its form changes.

q: Which is a renewable source?
solution: Wind is replenished naturally.

q: Why is a machine never 100% efficient?
solution: Some energy is always lost as heat due to friction and other effects.

topic: Nature of Sound and Its Propagation
q: Sound waves are:
solution: Sound waves cause compressions and rarefactions along the direction of travel.

topic: Nature of Sound and Its Propagation
q: Ultrasound has frequency:
solution: Ultrasound lies above the human audible range.

topic: Nature of Sound and Its Propagation
q: Why can't sound travel through a vacuum?
solution: Sound needs particles to vibrate and carry energy; a vacuum has no particles.

q: An echo is due to:
solution: Sound reflects from surfaces.

q: Sonar uses:
solution: Sonar sends ultrasound pulses and measures echoes.

q: What is reverberation?
solution: The persistence of sound in a hall due to repeated reflections from walls and ceiling.

q: Which is an infectious disease?
solution: Malaria is caused by a pathogen and is transmitted by mosquitoes.

q: Non-infectious diseases are caused by:
solution: They do not involve a transmissible pathogen.

q: Define health.
solution: A state of complete physical, mental and social well-being, not merely the absence of disease.

q: Antibiotics are effective against:
solution: Antibiotics target bacterial structures and processes.

q: A vaccine works by:
solution: It creates memory cells that respond quickly to infection.

q: Name three measures to prevent communicable diseases.
solution: Vaccination, safe drinking water and good hygiene (also vector control).

q: Which gas forms the ozone layer?
solution: Ozone absorbs harmful ultraviolet radiation.

q: Rising carbon dioxide mainly contributes to:
solution: Carbon dioxide is a greenhouse gas.

q: Why is the ozone layer important?
solution: It absorbs UV radiation that would harm living organisms.

q: The variety of life on Earth is called:
solution: Biodiversity is the variety of genes, species and ecosystems.

q: Sustainable development means:
solution: It balances present and future needs.
options: Meeting present needs without harming future generations

q: Give two examples of ecosystem services.
solution: Pollination of crops and water purification by wetlands.

q: Which nutrient helps in forming proteins in plants?
solution: Nitrogen is essential for protein and chlorophyll synthesis.

q: Manure is a:
solution: Manure is decomposed organic matter.

q: Why is crop rotation with legumes beneficial?
solution: Legumes fix atmospheric nitrogen, improving soil fertility and breaking pest cycles.

q: Rearing of honeybees is called:
solution: Apiculture is beekeeping.

q: Which of these improves milk yield in cattle?
solution: Selective breeding improves productivity.

q: Name two products of apiculture.
solution: Honey and beeswax (and pollination service).
